description: One synthesized row is read, displayed and the file ends orderly, so the run completes normally with RETURN-CODE 0 - and the row is what makes this case additive: it is the only row in this folder whose CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME AND CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE ARE BOTH ENTIRELY BLANK, which states the PIC X(50) and PIC X(10) spans at their LOWER boundary exactly as case13 states the name span at its upper one. INTERIOR SPACE RUNS ARE DATA, NOT ABSENCE. With both fields blanked, one-based offsets 31 TO 90 FORM SIXTY CONSECUTIVE SPACES, then CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS 'Y' at 91, then FILLER's fifty-nine spaces at 92-150: the LAST 119 CHARACTERS OF THE IMAGE ARE SPACES EXCEPT FOR THAT SINGLE 'Y'. Every one of those spaces is a stored byte of a stored field, and the whole point of the case is that a translation cannot tell them apart from padding by looking at them. A codec that trimmed the name, collapsed the run, normalised repeated blanks, or decided that a blank PIC X field is absent and dropped it to null would shorten the image and DRAG EVERY OFFSET AFTER IT LEFT - the status byte would arrive from 31 instead of 91 and the row would no longer measure 150 at all. This is therefore the strongest whitespace-fidelity assertion in the directory, and it exists alongside two neighbours that each state a weaker part of it: case09 pins the trailing FILLER span, which a trim would eat from the right; case13 pins a name span filled to all fifty bytes, where there is nothing to pad and nothing to truncate. Between the three, the X(50) span is asserted empty, full, and untouched. THE NON-SPACE CENSUS, stated exactly because it is easy to state loosely: the image carries a THIRTY-CHARACTER LEADING RUN of non-space characters - CARD-NUM, CARD-ACCT-ID and CARD-CVV-CD, 16+11+3 = 30 - PLUS THE SINGLE non-space status byte at 91, so THIRTY-ONE non-space characters in the whole 150, and 119 spaces. The 30 and the 1 are counted separately rather than added up loosely, because a lone total of 30 would silently license blanking the status byte, and the status byte is one of the ninety bytes this case inherits unchanged. NO VALIDATION, NO DEFAULTING, NO SUBSTITUTION (practice B5). CBACT02C INSPECTS NO RECORD FIELD AT ALL: grep over app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl finds zero references to CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME, CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE or CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS anywhere in the program, and its entire decision surface is three IF CARDFILE-STATUS tests - :94 in the read, :121 in the open, :139 in the close - the nested IF CARDFILE-STATUS = '10' at :98, the two IF END-OF-FILE = 'N' guards at :75 and :77, the 88-level tests of APPL-AOK VALUE 0 and APPL-EOF VALUE 16 declared at :62-63 and read at :104, :107, :126 and :144, and the two-armed condition at :162-163 inside 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS. Not one of them looks at a field of CARD-RECORD. So a blank name and a blank expiry date are displayed EXACTLY AS STORED: no 'MISSING', no 'N/A', no substituted default date, no rejection, no warning line, no reject file and no non-zero return code. A translation that added any of those would be adding a feature, and the added line would appear among the three expected below and be reported as a difference. CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE IS PIC X(10), NOT A DATE TYPE. app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy:9 declares it CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE - EXPIRAION, missing the second T - and that misspelling is preserved verbatim here and never corrected, because field-for-field diffing keys on the field name (AAP implicit requirement I1); CVACT01Y:11 misspells its own ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE the same way, so the spelling is the schema's, not a typo in one file. The picture matters as much as the spelling: TEN SPACES IS A PERFECTLY LEGAL VALUE FOR AN X(10) SPAN, and this case seeds precisely that. It is the substantive reason the Java model must keep the field a String - a java.time.LocalDate could not hold ten spaces at all, so modelling the field as a date would make this legal row unrepresentable, and the failure would arrive as a parse exception on real data rather than as a difference in a line. Nothing in CBACT02C parses that span either, so the blank date needs no handling of any kind here: the field is carried, displayed, and nothing more. THE DERIVATION, exactly: SYNTHESIZED FROM app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt ROW 1 BY BLANKING ONE-BASED OFFSETS 31-80 (CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME PIC X(50), FIFTY SPACES) AND ONE-BASED OFFSETS 81-90 (CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE PIC X(10), TEN SPACES); THE OTHER NINETY BYTES ARE UNCHANGED - CARD-NUM 0500024453765740 at 1-16, CARD-ACCT-ID 00000000050 at 17-27, CARD-CVV-CD 747 at 28-30, CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS Y at 91, and FILLER's fifty-nine spaces at 92-150. The two blanked ranges come from the copybook's cumulative layout rather than from eyeballing a fixture line (practice B11), and the assembled row is measured programmatically: 150 characters, offsets 1-30 byte-identical to the fixture row, offsets 31-90 exactly sixty spaces, offset 91 'Y', offsets 92-150 exactly fifty-nine spaces. Because the fixture row already carried spaces inside its own name span, THE HAMMING DISTANCE FROM THAT ROW IS EIGHTEEN rather than sixty: the eight non-space characters of 'Aniya Von' and the ten characters of '2023-03-09' are all that change, while the inter-word space at position 36 and the forty-one trailing spaces of the name span at 40-80 already agreed. The differences run from position 31 to position 90 and NOWHERE ELSE IN THE ROW, which is asserted mechanically rather than claimed. THE MUTATION LIVES ONLY IN THIS FILE (practice B3): app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt and its byte-identical classpath copy at src/test/resources/fixtures/carddata.txt are read-only parity oracle and are NOT edited to add a blank-field row - all fifty fixture rows carry a populated name and a populated date, the shortest trimmed name in the whole file being NINE characters and it being this very row's own 'Aniya Von', the longest nineteen - so no fromRow and rowCount range over the fixture can reach a blank one. The inline rows member exists for exactly this need, and the row is seeded verbatim with its sixty interior spaces and its fifty-nine trailing ones written out as real characters rather than as a marker, a repeat count or a comment (practice B1). THE RUN, into app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl:70-87 and nowhere else. :71 displays the 38-character start banner. :72 performs 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN, whose OPEN INPUT at :120 reports '00', so :121 takes its first arm, :122 moves 0 into APPL-RESULT and :126-127 CONTINUE. The PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y' at :74-81 begins: :75 finds 'N', :76 performs 1000-CARDFILE-GET-NEXT, the READ at :93 delivers the row into CARD-RECORD and reports '00', :94 takes its first arm and :95 moves 0 into APPL-RESULT - :96's DISPLAY CARD-RECORD is A COMMENT and emits nothing - then :104 finds the 88-level APPL-AOK true and CONTINUEs at :105. Back in the mainline :77 finds END-OF-FILE still 'N', so :78 DISPLAYs the whole 150-byte record area, once, blanks included. The second iteration re-enters at :75, :76 performs the read paragraph again, and the READ at :93 reports '10': :94 falls through, :98 matches, :99 moves 16 into APPL-RESULT, :104 finds APPL-AOK false, :107 finds APPL-EOF true and :108 moves 'Y' into END-OF-FILE - the only MOVE to that field in the whole program. :77 now finds 'Y' so NO SECOND IMAGE IS DISPLAYED, the loop condition at :74 ends the loop, :83 performs 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE whose CLOSE at :138 reports '00' so :139 takes its first arm and :140 subtracts APPL-RESULT from itself to zero, :144-145 CONTINUE, :85 displays the 36-character end banner and :87 GOBACK leaves RETURN-CODE at 0. No error text, no status line and no 'ABENDING PROGRAM' appears, because :110-113, :129-132 and :147-150 are all unreached and 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM at :154-158 never runs. REPOSITORY SEQUENCE (gate G47): startBrowse '00', then readNext '00' delivering the row, then readNext '10' at end of file, then endBrowse '00'. Four calls and four statuses, in that order: the terminating '10' is a NORMAL outcome here and not an error - it is the one terminator of the three-armed read paragraph that does not reach :101. That is what separates this case from the ten in this folder that abend; the twenty split ten normal completions against ten abends. The job is driven at TASKLET AND STEP LEVEL through the tasklet body itself, with NO JobLauncher, no job repository, no step execution context and no HTTP anywhere in the path (gate G51), so the three lines below are the program's own SYSOUT and not a framework's rendering of it. MESSAGE ARITHMETIC: 1 start banner + 1 record image + 1 end banner = THREE ordered DISPLAY_LINE entries, of 38, 150 and 36 characters. ONE IMAGE PER RECORD, exactly one, because :96's DISPLAY inside 1000-CARDFILE-GET-NEXT is commented out and there is no 1100-DISPLAY paragraph anywhere in the file, so :78 is the program's only live display of a record; a translation that re-displayed the row from inside the read paragraph would emit four lines and be caught here. The two banners are the byte-exact literals of :71 and :85 and are compared against the production constants rather than against each other. RECORD GEOMETRY, taken mechanically from app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy (01 CARD-RECORD, RECLN 150), one-based with cumulative ends: CARD-NUM PIC X(16) at 1-16, cumulative 16, and also the RECORD KEY at :32; CARD-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11) at 17-27, cumulative 27; CARD-CVV-CD PIC 9(03) at 28-30, cumulative 30 - which is what puts CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME at 31, since 16+11+3 = 30; CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME PIC X(50) at 31-80, cumulative 80; CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE PIC X(10) at 81-90, cumulative 90; CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS PIC X(01) at 91, cumulative 91; FILLER PIC X(59) at 92-150, cumulative 150. 16+11+3+50+10+1+59 = 150 (gate G19), and FILLER's fifty-nine significant spaces are emitted and never trimmed (gate G21) - which on this row is indistinguishable by eye from the sixty that precede the status byte, and is exactly why both are measured rather than inspected. The copybook declares no COMP-3, no PACKED-DECIMAL and no S9, so both numeric spans are unsigned zoned DISPLAY and there is no sign overpunch to model on a card record at all. WHAT THIS CASE PINS ABOUT THE UNIT: it is account.AccountBalanceReaderJob - an Account-named class in the account package - yet CBACT02C computes no balance and never opens the account file. IT READS THE CARD FILE. :29-33 is SELECT CARDFILE-FILE ASSIGN TO CARDFILE, ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED, ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL, RECORD KEY IS FD-CARD-NUM, FILE STATUS IS CARDFILE-STATUS; :37-40 is an FD of FD-CARD-NUM X(16) plus FD-CARD-DATA X(134) = 150; and :45 is COPY CVACT02Y. AAP rule R1 governs - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - and the divergence is catalogued in the register at AAP 0.8.4. A reviewer who trusts the class name will look for the wrong file and for arithmetic this program does not contain. WIRING: app/jcl/READCARD.jcl:22 is a bare //STEP05 EXEC PGM=CBACT02C, the job declares no PARM anywhere and CBACT02C has no LINKAGE SECTION to receive one into, so jobParameters is empty; its single //CARDFILE DD at :25-26 is the only dataset seeded, addressed solely by the CARDFILE binding key that application.yml resolves at record length 150 with copybook CVACT02Y, so no dataset-name literal appears anywhere in this file (gate G46). ENCODING IS US-ASCII, named explicitly rather than left to a platform default, and this row earns the naming more than most: 119 of its 150 bytes are spaces, and the space is 0x20 under US-ASCII but 0x40 under IBM037, so the bytes this whole assertion rests on are only determinate once the code page is stated (practice B8). NOTHING IS WRITTEN: expectedWrites and expectedFinalState are empty, and that emptiness is a positive assertion rather than an absence of interest - :120 opens the file INPUT and the program contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE at all, its only output being SYSOUT at app/jcl/READCARD.jcl:27. No normalisation is declared: this row is already the full 150 bytes CVACT02Y declares, so neither recorded fixture-to-copybook deviation applies, and in particular the cardxref 36-to-50 pad has no subject on a card record. DETERMINISM (practice B7): two documented byte-range blankings over one fixture row, no wall-clock, no random source, no environment lookup, and ordered lists throughout, so the case produces the same three lines on every run and on every machine. The blank expiry date in particular must NOT tempt an implementation into substituting today's date, a sentinel or a zero-filled date: the COBOL stores ten spaces, displays ten spaces, and any clock reading in that span would make the expected image untestable as well as wrong. PROVENANCE: every expected value in this file is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl, cross-checked against app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy for every offset and width, app/jcl/READCARD.jcl for the step and DD contract, and the real app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt for the ninety bytes this row inherits verbatim. It was NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from a live COBOL execution: AAP 0.7.6 proves such a run impossible in this environment with eight independently verified blockers - no z/OS runtime, the available compiler's indexed file handler disabled, subprogram linkage that cannot be made executable, a copybook that will not parse, no Language Environment CEE services, no CICS emulator alongside three absent IBM copybooks, EBCDIC fixtures needing binary handling, and no alternative compiler installable - and the substitution of provenance is recorded as risk R-A (practice B12). Only the provenance changes; the twenty cases, the field-for-field diff and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand. GATES PINNED HERE: G15 (one of the twenty cases for this program), G18 (its diff count must be zero), G19 and G21 (the 150-byte width holding with both alphanumeric spans blank, and FILLER's fifty-nine significant spaces surviving beside sixty more that are not FILLER), G46 (binding key, never a DSNAME), G47 (the four-status sequence ending in a clean '10' and a clean endBrowse) and G51 (asserted below the HTTP and JobLauncher layers). NOT APPLICABLE: G30 and G32, since CBACT02C contains no GO TO; G33, since it declares no OCCURS; G16 and both right-pad normalisations, since carddata.txt needs neither; G20, since this program writes no record; G22 through G28, since CVACT02Y declares no V99 span and this program performs no arithmetic beyond its own status bookkeeping, so the BigDecimal and RoundingMode.DOWN gates have no subject here; G35, since nothing on this path reaches CALL 'CEE3ABD'; and G37 through G43, since no screen is driven. One row seeded whose name and expiry date are both entirely blank, one delivered, one displayed byte for byte, three lines out, RETURN-CODE 0.
